_schema.applies_to: matcher on {program, metrics, subgroups}; null = any
_schema.basis: traceability: the bulletin supporting documentation, the ready-reckoner bulletin, a GitHub issue, or a measured diagnostic in this repo's data

annotations.text: Ready-reckoner rows are reform deltas, not levels: direct effects against HMRC's indexed baseline under the OBR Spring Statement 2025 forecast, implemented April 2026. A PE counterpart must run the same nominal change against a matching indexed baseline and state the baseline explicitly (#13). The asymmetric (cost)/(yield) row pairs are distinct claims — behavioural response differs by direction — and must not be averaged.
annotations.basis: Direct effects bulletin June 2025; scorecard issue #13

annotations.text: Direct effects include HMRC's specified behavioural adjustments (e.g. taxable income elasticities for additional-rate changes), not pure static costings. A static PE run is the right first counterpart but is expected to exceed HMRC yield estimates where elasticities bite; classify that wedge as construction, not model error. The campaign's hmrc_reckoner_t2 family already carries PE static counterparts for Table 2 rows.

2023-24 is the latest SPI outturn year; 2024-25 to 2026-27 are HMRC projections on OBR-consistent economic assumptions, not measurements. Score projected years as forecast-vs-forecast (both models project), and expect revisions when the next SPI lands.

An Income Tax payer is an individual with positive liability after allowances and reliefs; marginal-rate bands follow HMRC's classification (savers rate = savings/dividend-rate payers; Scottish rates fold into the nearest rUK band). The PE counterpart is individuals with income_tax > 0, banded by marginal rate on the same definitions — not adults, not benefit units.

Liabilities are accrued amounts for the tax year, not cash receipts (HMRC receipts statistics and OBR receipts forecasts differ by timing and non-SPI elements). Compare PE income tax liability aggregates against these rows, never against receipts outturns.

Counts are rounded (thousands at varying precision), liabilities to £ millions; '[no estimate]' marks small-sample cells and 'Neg' marks reckoner effects that round to zero — both carried as suppressed. Table 2.1 pre-2009-10 years reflect historical band structures ('[not applicable]' cells are skipped, not suppressed).
UK-total rows include Scottish and Welsh taxpayers under their devolved rates. PE UK models devolved income tax; comparisons are UK-total here, and per-country rows wait on Table 2.2 emission.
